text:
Simon Holmstrom has turned a fourth-line demotion into the best stretch of his career, in a contract year. He has points in seven straight games (six goals, five assists), including a hat trick in Anaheim, and NHL.com's Stefen Rosner is already asking the question: "Is Simon Holmstrom's hot streak just who he is now?"

Part of it is. He plays 18:09 a night, up from 16:44, is on the ice for 48% of the Islanders' power-play chances after 19% last season, and his own chances are up to 0.91 expected goals per 60 from 0.66. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries, and carry-ins create far more chances than dump-ins.

The finishing is the part that won't last. Ten goals on 6.0 expected means a 26% shooting rate, above even last season's 19%, and New York has scored 5.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our range for his finishing tops out at 19.1%. The new role looks sturdy; the goal pace probably isn't. Our numbers project 57 points and 25 goals.
headline: Holmstrom turned a demotion into a contract-year run
